result.title: Prescriptive Learning of Linear Policies with Feasibility Guarantees for Binary Decision-Making
result.summary: Binary decision-making under uncertainty arises across a wide range of applications, including energy systems scheduling, transportation, and workforce planning. While machine learning has been increasingly applied to accelerate or replace mixed-integer solvers in such settings, existing approaches rely on predictive learning, training models to reproduce optimal decisions from labeled data, which lacks knowledge of counterfactual outcomes and provides no guarantees that the resulting decisions will be feasible. This limitation is further compounded under distributional shift, where policies trained on historical data may produce systematically infeasible decisions. We propose a prescriptive learning framework for binary decision-making that addresses both limitations. Rather than predicting optimal labels, the framework jointly optimizes over linear decision policies and feasible assignments across all training scenarios, allowing feasible alternatives and their operational performance to be considered directly during training. We further extend the framework to a distributionally robust chance-constrained formulation using a Wasserstein ambiguity set, which enforces feasibility with a prescribed probability under the worst-case distribution in the ambiguity set and enables a tunable trade-off between robustness and solution quality. We demonstrate the framework on two case studies, namely a unit commitment problem and a staff allocation problem. Out-of-sample experiments under test distributions that either match or differ from the training distribution show that the robust model is more conservative when the two distributions coincide, while under distributional shift it substantially reduces unmet demand and lowers total cost by up to 76.5% relative to classical predictive learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出面向不确定性下二值决策的 prescriptive learning 框架，在训练中联合优化线性决策策略与各场景的可行分配，并扩展为基于 Wasserstein 模糊集的分布鲁棒机会约束形式，在机组组合与人员配置案例中检验分布偏移下的可行性与成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「模仿最优标签的预测式学习 vs 直接优化下游决策并施加可行性/鲁棒约束」的对比，可能与 LVR 中 latent 轨迹究竟以模仿推理标签还是以下游决策收益为监督目标的问题构成类比，可供核查；但材料不含视觉或多模态状态，联系较远。
